subject.title: fix: protect SMS webhook callback quota [AI]

question: Should the SMS webhook ship a separate 300 failed requests/minute budget per account-route-client key with a 5,000-key bounded-memory limit, while retaining the 30/min dispatch cap?
rationale: The implementation and proof establish the mechanics, but the allowed unauthenticated workload and bounded-key behavior are security and availability policy choices that require owner intent.

options.title: Accept current policy
options.body: Ship the proved 300/min failure budget, 30/min dispatch cap, and 5,000-key bounds as the intended abuse-versus-availability balance.

options.title: Retune the bounds
options.body: Keep the two-stage design but change the failed-request threshold or tracked-key limit and repeat the same-client reverse-proxy proof.

options.title: Reject split quotas
options.body: Retain the current single gate and accept that invalid traffic can consume capacity needed by valid callbacks.

recommendation.title: Accept current policy
recommendation.body: Ship the proved 300/min failure budget, 30/min dispatch cap, and 5,000-key bounds as the intended abuse-versus-availability balance.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the SMS webhook’s original security and quota contract and recently reviewed and landed adjacent webhook hardening.
